sentences: In the golden evening light, an old warship makes her final voyage.
This is The Fighting Temeraire, shown by Turner at the Royal Academy in 1839.
Its full title says she is being tugged to her last berth to be broken up.
The Temeraire, a ship of 98 guns, had helped protect Nelson's flagship at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.
Here, in 1838, she is being towed up the River Thames to a London shipbreaker's yard, to be broken up for scrap.
The old warship is painted in pale, almost ghostly colours.
In reality her masts and rigging had been removed before the sale, but Turner kept her tall masts standing, as she would have looked in her days of glory.
High in the sky at the upper left, a faint crescent moon rises, casting a thin, silvery path of light down onto the water.
With the sunset and the moon in one sky, the end of the day and the start of night overlap.
Turner placed the tug's funnel in front of its mast, so the black smoke trails back past the pale, ghostly masts of the old sailing ship.
The smoke's reddish glow echoes the clouds of the sunset.
Leading the way is a squat, dark steam tugboat.
In fact two tugs had to tow her, but Turner painted only one, setting the old and the new face to face.
It is a small, busy boat dragging a silent giant.
In the river below, the red clouds and the dark shadows of the ships are mirrored.
Sky and water flow together until the whole canvas seems to shimmer, and loose, visible brushstrokes break the glow into ripples.
Opposite, on the right side of the picture, a blazing sunset sets the sky on fire.
The sun could not really set in that direction on this stretch of river, but Turner matched it to the ship's fate.
He chose meaning over literal fact.
The whole sky becomes a picture of the age of sail beginning to give way to the age of steam.
A glorious past is yielding to a new machine, and the scene holds both regret and awe at once.
Turner called the painting his darling.
He refused to sell it, and when he died he left it to the nation.
The novelist Thackeray called it as grand a picture as any academy had ever hung.
In 2005 it was voted Britain's favourite painting in a BBC radio poll, and it now appears behind Turner's own self-portrait on the Bank of England's £20 note.
Step back and ask yourself: is this evening an ending, or a beginning?
